summary: Compilation, caching and process ownership are specified closely enough to build, but the conversational ExecuteGuest contract (callback semantics, termination, returned bytes) is undefined and is the biggest gap.

questions.text: What does the ExecuteGuest callback receive (raw chunks or de-framed requests), and what does a Nothing result mean for ending the conversation?
questions.reason: Determines the conversation loop, its termination and abort semantics; the ADR gives only the type and defers framing to ADR 0007, defining Nothing only for ReadStdout (EOF).

questions.text: What is the String argument of executeCompiledEntry, given the entry is already fixed in the CompiledProgram?
questions.reason: Decides whether one artifact holds several runtime-selected entries (changing bytecode and launch configuration) or the string is only diagnostic context; the ADR says only that the helper maps nonzero exit to RuntimeUnavailable.

questions.text: Which channel reports GuestSources validation failures (duplicate paths, collisions, missing entry): smart-constructor error, Left [Diagnostic], or Failure?
questions.reason: Places the check in the domain package or the interpreter and classifies it as authoring diagnostic or operational fault; the ADR lists the checks but only classifies compiler exit statuses.

questions.text: What environment, locale and working directory does the mhseval process get at execution time?
questions.reason: ProcessSpec needs a complete environment and guest text I/O depends on locale; the ADR fixes the compiler environment (MHSDIR, MHSCPPHS, empty PATH, C.UTF-8) but says only that execution's launch configuration comes from the toolchain.

questions.text: Where does the checkout-local Dhall inspection cache live, and is the checkout the KB repository or the Kyyn source tree?
questions.reason: Decides directory plumbing, gitignore handling and whether release builds cache inspection; the ADR says only 'checkout-local' and lists the key inputs.

questions.text: Where does toolchainRevision come from, and is the compiled-artifact cache disabled when it is unknown (e.g. plain Cabal builds)?
questions.reason: It is part of the fingerprint and cache key, so its source decides stale-artifact reuse; the ADR says it identifies the pinned MicroHs source and disables only inspection caching for unidentified builds.

questions.text: Does 'equivalent bytecode' between gmhs and self-hosted mhs mean byte-identical .comb output or behavioural equivalence?
questions.reason: Defines the parity guarantee and whether the cache key can ignore which compiler build produced an artifact; the ADR only says full integration checks this parity.

questions.text: What path validation or normalization does GuestSources apply (absolute paths, '..', '.', empty segments, non-UTF-8 names)?
questions.reason: Unnormalized paths give one tree two digests and could escape the build scope; the ADR defines the digest over sorted length-delimited paths and case-sensitive collision checks only.

questions.text: How does application composition locate the installed toolchain to build GuestToolchain (relative to the executable, embedded prefix, env override)?
questions.reason: Sets resolution code, missing-toolchain failure and dev/test overrides; the ADR rules out ambient PATH and names the bin/mhs install path but not how it is resolved.

questions.text: Is a corrupt inspection cache entry a hard failure or a reported miss that is recomputed?
questions.reason: Changes control flow and user experience; the ADR says corrupt cache diagnostics identify the entry to remove, implying but not stating a failure.

questions.text: Does toolchainRevision cover only the MicroHs compiler source or also cpphs, mhseval and the base/SDK libraries?
questions.reason: A preprocessor-only bump could reuse stale artifacts; the ADR says the revision identifies the MicroHs source yet treats library/preprocessor as part of the pinned toolchain.

questions.text: Which fixed CPP defines are passed to the compiler?
questions.reason: They select SDK/dependency code paths and are part of the cache key; the ADR mentions 'fixed CPP defines' without naming them.

questions.text: Are there size limits on guest stdout, stderr and compiler output, and what happens when one is exceeded?
questions.reason: Unbounded buffering lets a runaway guest exhaust host memory; the ADR says output is drained and returned as bytes with no limit.

questions.text: What are the returned Bytes of ExecuteGuest in conversational mode: the final framed result, leftover stdout, or all stdout?
questions.reason: Decides what callers receive and how results are mapped; the ADR gives only the (Bytes, ProcessExit) result type.
